conventions.convention: P is row-stochastic: P_xy = Pr(y | x), and row distributions evolve as μP. The empty state set is allowed, but has no probability distribution.
A finite reversible chain supplies a normalized stationary law with every π_x strictly positive and detailed balance. Irreducibility and aperiodicity are not assumed.
The root inner product is linear first. T prepares nonnegative square-root row amplitudes in ordered product bases, S swaps the two factors, and D = T*ST. Empty label spaces are zero spaces.
The absolute gap is 1 minus the operator norm on the weighted mean-zero subspace. A zero restriction has norm zero, so the one-state chain has gap one.
R_A = 2TT* − I, U = SR_A, and W = U²; products act right to left. The opposite reflection sign cannot be substituted inside controlled operations.

Circuit access requires a nonempty encoded state set and a supplied clean-work row-preparation unitary. Forward, inverse, controlled, reflection and swap capabilities and their resource coordinates are separately declared.

load_bearing.statement: For every finite row-stochastic kernel, T*T = I, T is an isometry, D_xy = √(P_xy P_yx), and D is real symmetric, self-adjoint and contractive. For a supplied finite reversible chain, D = diag(√π) P diag(1/√π).

Each discriminant eigendirection with λ ∈ (−1,1) contributes exp(±i arccos λ) to U and exp(±2i arccos λ) to W. Each λ = ±1 eigendirection contributes one line with U eigenvalue λ and W eigenvalue +1. On K = (ran T + ran(ST))⊥, U = −S has eigenvalues only ±1 and W is identity. Empty-state eigenvalue assertions are vacuous.

For a nonempty chain in the supplied row-preparation implementation, SV_P R_0 V_P* restricts on clean work to U. This implementation uses one inverse preparation, one clean-state reflection, one forward preparation and one swap; factorwise control controls every constituent, and W uses two such U implementations.
For Dv = λv with v ≠ 0 and λ ∈ [−1,1], a = Tv and b = STv satisfy Ua = b and Ub = −a + 2λb. Their span is invariant, one-dimensional at λ = ±1 and two-dimensional for |λ| < 1.
For a finite reversible chain, the absolute gap is one when H_0 = {0}; otherwise it is 1 − max{|λ| : λ ∈ σ(P restricted to H_0)} and belongs to [0,1]. A nonconstant fixed function forces gap zero.
For a finite reversible chain, P is self-adjoint for the weighted inner product, the mean-zero subspace H_0 is invariant, and its restriction is self-adjoint.

concerns.concern: Steps 1.3, 1.4 and 3.1 use σ(U) and σ(W) for eigenvalue multisets, for example “σ(U)={1,1,1,−1}”. The cited def-eigenvalue-eigenvector-eigenspace-and-spectrum defines σ as a set, which discards multiplicity. The requested multiset computations and their numerical multiplicities are correct, but this notation conflicts with the cited convention.

seams_checked.note: The access definition treats uniform generation as additional supplied input and preserves separate description, generator, gate, query and precision coordinates.
Ordered product bases and swap conventions agree. Empty label spaces are explicitly zero spaces; circuit access is restricted to nonempty state sets.
Root pairings remain linear first; the discriminant entry proof includes the required conjugation, and rank-one operators use the supplied Dirac conversion.
Reflection signs agree, and controlled and inverse access are explicit separate capabilities. Factorwise control includes every constituent.
Walk words act right to left, consistently with chronological circuit denotation. Matrix data alone is not claimed to supply circuit access or efficient implementation.

Checked the absorbing discriminant, search and detection spectral uses, Johnson gap and row-access uses. Detection uses U phases and finding uses W phases; endpoint and complement behavior, positive stationary-law hypotheses and controlled preparation costs are preserved.
